correctness.rationale: The original graph-metric Rips convention includes edges at distance one. An invariant simplex has barycentric coordinates constant on ground-set-transposition vertex orbits; singleton A_P, singleton D_Q and paired C_S orbits give an honest geometric fixed orbit complex, not merely the fixed-vertex subcomplex. Distinct C_S are incompatible, and every C_S is coned onto one star simplex in Cl(J(m,k)) and one top simplex in Cl(J(m,k-2)); replacement by N=C(m,k-1) bridges yields N-1 fundamental circles. The smaller Johnson complexes collapse by unique maximal-star/top ownership of triangles to simply connected two-complexes with V=C(m,j), E=j(m-j)V/2 and T=C(m,j-1)C(m-j,2)+C(m,j+1)C(j,2), so Hurewicz and Whitehead give wedges of b(m,j) two-spheres including j=1,m-1 simplex boundaries. An independently coded orbit-complex chain construction yields reduced F2 Betti vectors (0,5,0) at (6,3), (0,9,4) at (7,3), (0,19,20) at (8,4), and (0,34,75) at (9,4), with no other reduced homology. These finite checks corroborate but do not replace the all-parameter collapse and homotopy proof.
